testCases.input: what is vibe testing and why isn't it enough for deploying an llm app?
testCases.actualOutput:
Vibe testing is a very informal way of checking an LLM‑based application. Think of it as a quick “feel‑good” check: you fire off a handful of prompts—usually five to ten—read the answers, and decide whether the system seems to be working just by the way it feels. It’s subjective, it’s not repeatable (the next time you’ll ask different questions), and it’s usually done only at the personal project level. Because of that, it never produces a production‑ready assessment.

That’s why vibe testing alone isn’t enough for deploying an LLM app. First, the evaluation is not objective; you’re relying on a single person’s impression rather than measurable metrics. Second, it can’t be repeated reliably—if you run the same test a week later you’ll likely ask different questions and get different results, so you can’t guarantee consistency. Third, it doesn’t expose the system to the wide variety of real‑world user interactions that a production chatbot will face; the case studies of Air Canada and others show that a system that passes a quick vibe test can still hallucinate or give wrong answers when users ask more varied or nuanced questions. Finally, the industry expects a more rigorous, automated offline evaluation that can be integrated into CI/CD pipelines, with clear thresholds (like a 95 % score) before a release is allowed. Vibe testing is a useful sanity check for early prototypes, but it lacks the repeatability, objectivity, and coverage needed to ensure a reliable, production‑grade LLM application.
